notes.1: This question can be solved in a number of different ways. The most popular approach was to use horizontal and vertical motion to find the two velocities. Having done this the resultant of these is equal to 18. This leads directly to the required time. Answer: 1.1(0) s
notes.2i: This part was done by equating vertically for the particle.
notes.2ii: By using Newton’s Second Law in the direction of the centre O, the required velocity was found.
notes.3: To solve this question candidates were required to use horizontal and vertical motion. The horizontal and vertical velocities at A are Vcosθ and Vsinθ. Horizontal motion gives 40 cos30 = Vcosθ x 4 i.e. Vcosθ = 10 cos30 Vertical motion gives 40 sin30 =Vsinθ x 4 – x 10 x 4 i.e. Vsinθ = 25. By squaring and adding these V can be found and by dividing θ can be found. Answers: V = 26.5 and θ = 70.9
notes.6ii: This part of the question can be solved by taking moments. If moments are taken about the vertex of the cone then 4 x 0.6 + W x 0.9 = (4 + W) x 0.85. This leads to W = 20.
